CHUGTER SERIES
The Chugter series consists of deep, gently sloping to moderately steep, well-drained soils on fans, footslopes and terraces in shallow valleys. Slopes range from 2 to 15 percent. They formed in loam and gravelly loam alluvium from mixed calcareous sedimentary rocks at elevations of 3400 to 4000 feet.
The vegetation is western wheatgrass, sideoats, grama, needle-and-thread, prairie junegrass, big sagebrush and cheatgrass. The annual precipitation is 11 to 13 inches, the mean annual soil temperature is 46 to 48 degrees F., and the frost free season is 115 to 130 days.
Typically, the surface layer is reddish brown loam about 6 inches thick. The subsoil is reddish brown loam about 23 inches thick. The substratum is light reddish brown loam to 60 or more inches.
The soil has moderate to moderately rapid permeability. The effective rooting depth is 60 or more inches. Available water holding capacity is 10 to 12 inches.
These soils are used for range and dry cropland.
A typical profile of Chugter loam in grassland, 525 feet west and 380 feet south of the E1/4 corner of Sec. 10, T. 9 S., R. 40 E.
